Everything is done: the project is documented, merged and pushed, the research repo has a new entry, the repo is public, and the blog post is live. One mistake along the way: my blog commit also pushed another session's unfinished essay work to the live site.

**What was done**
- **Findings:** `docs/FINDINGS.md` maps every result across the project, which is now marked paused. [PR #1](https://github.com/polarizetech/sim-neural-memory/pull/1), [PR #2](https://github.com/polarizetech/sim-neural-memory/pull/2), [PR #3](https://github.com/polarizetech/sim-neural-memory/pull/3) and [PR #4](https://github.com/polarizetech/sim-neural-memory/pull/4) are all merged (as merge commits) and `main` is pushed.
- **Research repo** (pushed: `5f13a74`, `2852d25`, `5d86fc9`): one simulation entry under `audio-evoked-potentials/simulations/runs/`, tier `[SPEC-sim]`.
  - It records two model-level refutations: depletion keeps no sound-specific memory, and the published Stentor receptor model drains untrained responses under a synthesis block. It also records that spaced training helped in no model.
  - Four sources were added to the citation ledger. Three are marked read in full after I read them; Vogels 2011 stays abstract-only.
  - The research audit passes.
- **Code review:** three independent reviews, collected in `docs/REVIEW.md`.
  - No equation, unit or integration error was found.
  - Five findings change how committed results read, though no experiment's verdict flips:
    - The tape's "one positive" (rank order) was measured while the sound played and mostly reflects the input. It is not evidence of memory.
    - Recall delays are later than labelled.
    - The Hebbian arm's starting weight drifts even in silence. That makes its 30-minute timescale and its spacing comparison confounded.
    - E02's pass/fail rule has two readings. E02 still fails either way.
    - Some per-cell results were written as if they held across all cells at once.
  - Each correction is appended, dated, to the report it affects; nothing already published was rewritten.
- **Linting:** `ruff` with correctness rules only, plus a GitHub Actions check that passes on the public repo.
  - Fixed: 79 lint issues, a latent bug in how paired comparisons match seeds, and tests that would have passed on any error.
  - Missing private tools are now reported instead of crashing, where that's possible without changing any number. They still block exact re-runs; see the last list.
  - All 100 tests pass, and no committed number changed.
- **Cleanup:**
  - No credentials or tokens anywhere in the history.
  - Your messages in the session logs and the two matching PR comments had spelling and grammar fixed. Each edit is marked, and the override of the kit's never-edit rule is recorded in both experiments' deviation logs.
  - Git history is left as is, per your answer.
  - MIT `LICENSE` and a new public-facing README.
- **Public:** <https://github.com/polarizetech/sim-neural-memory> loads without a login.
- **Blog:** <https://polarize.tech/blog/a-network-built-to-lose/> is live, tier SPEC, and links to the repo. It first returned 404 because its timestamp was in the future; I moved it to 07:00.
- **Mistake:** my blog commit (`141a921`) also swept in the polarize.tech session's staged work: the "Every cell remembers" essay, a new essays section and layout, sidebar and config changes, and gate-script edits. I only added my two files but didn't check what was already staged. It's pushed and live. I haven't reverted anything, and I've messaged that session.

**What I need from you**
- **Should the swept-in essay work stay live?** It looked finished and passed the site's checks. If it wasn't ready, the polarize.tech session or I can revert those paths.

**Not done, and not blocked on you**
- The monorepo's `research` submodule pointer still pins an older commit. I didn't touch the shared checkout.
- Exact re-runs of the tape experiments, and of E01/E02 through their original scripts, still need the two private tools. The README and `docs/REVIEW.md` say so.

- **Essays unpublished:** the polarize.tech session had already done this in `7e2253f`, before your message reached me. Both essays and the essays index now return 404, and the "Thinking out loud" sidebar link is gone.
  - The files are still in the repo, marked unpublished, so they can come back once you've previewed the layout.
  - I made no essay changes myself.
- **Retitled** the post to "A RAG tool that keeps the model in check" (`e05369d`). The file is renamed too, so it has a new address: <https://polarize.tech/blog/a-rag-tool-that-keeps-the-model-in-check/>.
  - The old address now returns 404, with no redirect as you said. Nothing else on the site linked to it.
  - The site's checks pass, and I committed only the renamed file, as agreed with the other session.
